title: Subdivision–Ex adjunction on homotopy classes with Kan targets
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For simplicial sets $A,B$, put $[A,B]_{\mathrm e}=\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)$: maps $A\to B$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by pairs joined by a simplicial homotopy $A\times\Delta^1\to B$. Take $\operatorname{Sd}A$ to be the degreewise colimit over simplices of $A$ of the nerves of posets of nonempty subsets of the corresponding ordinals, and put $(\operatorname{Ex}B)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(N(\mathcal P_+([n])),B)$ with subset-image operators, as in [lem-coef-subdivision-face-poset-calculus]. For every small simplicial set $A$ and every Kan complex $Y$, $\operatorname{Ex}Y$ is Kan, and the natural subdivision–Ex adjunction induces a bijection
$$[\operatorname{Sd}A,Y]_{\mathrm e}\ \cong\ [A,\operatorname{Ex}Y]_{\mathrm e}.$$
More explicitly, two maps $\operatorname{Sd}A\to Y$ represent the same edge-generated homotopy class if and only if their adjoint maps $A\to\operatorname{Ex}Y$ do. The bijection is natural in $A$ and in maps between Kan targets $Y$.
